newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty soars further as foreigners buy bills.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty soars further as foreigners buy bills.

text.p: The zloty remained in record territory against the basket of currencies after breaking strong resistance at four percent from the partiy rate on large scale foreigner entry into Polish treasuries.

Dealers said the next resistance for the zloty could be at 4.3 percent from parity and that there were no short term factors which might halt the local unit's rise other than a central bank currency-buying intervention.
"We may see further zloty appreciation after it broke the four percent barrier...with foreigners likely entering Polish treasuries," said Tomasz Nowakowski from Bank Handlowy.
At 1100 GMT the zloty was quoted at 4.05/4.02 percent from the trading band centre against opening's 3.96/3.90 percent and Friday's close at 3.80/3.82 percent.
It was at 2.9195/00 to the dollar, down from opening's 2.9200/20 and at 1.7970/80 to the mark, up from 1.8003/13.

Some dealers said the central bank was not likely to try to cap the zloty's rise by purchasing currencies before February 5, the value date for a recent two-year fixed bond tender because such a move would aid foreign investors. @
Dealers also said that there may be substantial foreign investor demand at today's 800 million zloty primary T-bill auction, despite market expectations of stable yields.
Foreign demand for the zloty combined with increased outflows for monthly tax payments have pushed the money market's short term rates up some 0.3 point to around 22 percent.
"Rates have grown on increased demand for zlotys coming from abroad as well as on increased tax outflows," said Malgorzata Sikora, money market dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Rates were expected to rise further later this week as banks start to square required reserve positions for January. @
At 1125 GMT overnight deposits were quoted at 21.85/22.00 percent, up from opening's 21.50/21.75 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 21.90/22.15 percent, up from 21.60/21.75 percent.
